title: Virtual Threads
objectives: Explain what virtual threads are and the problem they solve
Contrast platform threads with virtual threads
Know what 'pinning' is and how to avoid it

sections.markdown: Virtual threads (Project Loom, finalized in Java 21) are lightweight threads managed by the JVM, not the OS. Millions can run concurrently, making blocking I/O code scale like async — without callbacks.

Virtual threads make the classic 'thread-per-request' model scale to millions of connections, ending the need for reactive/callback code purely for concurrency. Write simple blocking code; the JVM handles scheduling.
**Pinning**: blocking inside a synchronized block (or native call) pins the virtual thread to its carrier OS thread, killing the benefit. Prefer ReentrantLock over synchronized in hot I/O paths.

flashcards.front: What problem do virtual threads solve?
flashcards.back: They let simple blocking code scale to millions of concurrent tasks without OS-thread limits or reactive callbacks.
Platform = 1:1 with an OS thread (heavy). Virtual = many-to-few, JVM-scheduled, cheap, unmounts on blocking I/O.
When a virtual thread can't unmount (e.g., blocking in a synchronized block), holding its carrier thread — avoid in hot paths.

quiz.explain: The JVM multiplexes many virtual threads onto a few carrier OS threads.
Blocking I/O unmounts the carrier, so millions of I/O tasks scale cheaply.
synchronized blocks (and some native calls) prevent unmounting, pinning the virtual thread.

challenges.text: Launch 1,000,000 virtual threads that sleep, and observe memory vs platform threads.
Rewrite a fixed thread pool server to one-virtual-thread-per-request.
Detect pinning with -Djdk.tracePinnedThreads and fix it.
Benchmark throughput of reactive vs virtual-thread blocking style under load.
